children: The charge will apply to person-to-merchant transactions above Rs 2,000, while person-to-person transfers remain free

The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) will introduce a Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) of 0.4 per cent on person-to-merchant (P2M) Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions above Rs 2,000 from 15 October. The charge will be paid by merchants, while customers will not be charged for UPI transactions.

Person-to-person (P2P) UPI transfers will continue to remain free irrespective of the transaction value. The new framework marks a change from the zero-MDR regime that has applied to UPI merchant payments for more than six years.

UPI processed 24.51 billion transactions worth Rs 29.82 lakh crore in August 2026, compared with 23.66 billion transactions worth Rs 29.88 lakh crore in July. The network had 752 banks live on the platform in August.

The MDR framework includes exemptions for smaller merchants and selected categories. Merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month through UPI QR payments under the P2M classification will continue to pay zero MDR. QR-based merchant payments in rural and semi-urban areas will also remain exempt.
According to the government, around 4 per cent of merchant transactions will be affected by the new MDR, as most transactions are either below Rs 2,000 or qualify for the small-merchant exemption.

Railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, agricultural inputs and specified categories will attract a flat Rs 5 charge on transactions above Rs 2,000 instead of the percentage-based MDR. These categories account for around 17 per cent of P2M transaction volume and approximately 46 per cent of merchant UPI value, according to the government.
Transactions involving mutual funds, securities, stockbrokers and related entities will attract an MDR of 0.02 per cent, capped at Rs 300.

The MDR on regular transactions will be capped at Rs 300 for payments of Rs 75,000 and above. The revenue will be distributed among the institutions involved in processing the transaction, including the payer's bank, merchant-acquiring bank and payment service providers.
The change comes as UPI processes tens of billions of transactions each month, requiring continued spending on technology, cybersecurity, fraud monitoring and payment infrastructure.

Government incentives have previously supported the zero-MDR model. The Department of Financial Services recorded an outlay of Rs 3,637 crore under its FY2023-24 incentive scheme covering RuPay debit cards and low-value BHIM-UPI merchant transactions, including Rs 3,270 crore for BHIM-UPI.
Pine Labs CEO Amrish Rau said MDR would support investment in technology, cybersecurity, fraud prevention and reliability as UPI scales.

The Reserve Bank of India has described the MDR framework as a step towards the long-term sustainability of the digital payments ecosystem while reiterating that UPI transactions remain free for consumers.
The Finance Ministry has said UPI app providers cannot impose platform or hidden fees on users. Banks have also been advised to ensure merchants do not pass MDR charges on to customers.
NPCI and banks will therefore have to monitor whether merchants impose additional charges on customers. Merchant responses could also vary depending on transaction size and business category.

The government is also setting up a dedicated fund, financed through 5 per cent of total MDR collections, to support UPI adoption among small merchants. NPCI has said the structure will be finalised in consultation with the RBI within three months.
The new framework changes the way merchant-side UPI payments are funded while retaining zero-cost access for consumers and P2P transactions.
